Six people from the crowd were arrested that night with charges, including felony aggravated battery on a peace officer, resisting obstructing, felony attempting to disarm a peace officer, and criminal damage to property, criminal damage to property as one of them allegedly broke a door handle off a police squad. Using the surveillance footage, police were also able to identify the male who shot the victim as 29-year-old Adrian. He was charged with two counts of felony aggravated battery with a firearm and felony unlawful possession of a weapon by a felon. The legal proceedings of his case, as well as the six other suspects arrested are ongoing, and they are all presumed innocent unless proven guilty in a court of law. The victim who was shot was transported to a hospital in critical condition and latest reporting indicates he survived with major injuries and faces a long an arduous path to recovery. The more than nine minutes that ambulance and fire crews were blocked from safely accessing the victim may have contributed to the severity of the victim's injuries. There was a lot of use of force during this incident and it's no coincidence. Using data from 1.5 million calls for service, a study from tactical signs found that the biggest correlation related to use of force was the type of call officers were responding to. Furthermore, police responding to Vaughn's calls was one of the most common types of calls correlated with use of force. The speed of response also mattered with research indicating that fast responses were associated with higher force rates. The body cam footage is consistent with this research, showing what happens when officers respond to a violence call extremely quickly. A surprising statistic, the study also found, though, was that force was only used in 0.14% of all calls for service, making it quite rare. Use of force is a tool that most officers don't take lightly and use only when absolutely necessary. And looking at its involvement in cases like this, body camera footage helps us to understand the why of it all, and to be as prepared as possible for anything that may happen during a call. And I've also had to disperse hostile crowds like this. and officers can't even reach a gunshot victim without being attacked. That's not a policing problem. That's a community problem.

event_summary.short: A man was shot in Peoria, Illinois after an argument, and a large crowd hindered police response. The shooter was identified and charged, and six bystanders were arrested for interfering with officers.
